mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (عم): its origin is (عن ما). The alif was dropped because a preposition entered upon (ما), which is interrogative, to distinguish between the interrogative and the declarative; the fatḥa indicates the alif. Ibn Kathīr, in the transmission of al-Bazzī from him, paused on it with hāʾ to make the vowel clear, so that the alif would not be dropped and what indicates it dropped too. The body of the other readers paused with vowellessness. Likewise whatever resembles it of the interrogative (ما) when a preposition enters upon it: this is its rule. Keeping the alif is not permissible except in poetry, just as dropping the alif is not permissible when (ما) is declarative, as in (وما الله بغافل عما يعملون).

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (عن النبإ): a badal (substitute) from (ما) with the preposition repeated. It is also said that the implied form is "They ask one another about the news", then the verb was omitted because the first indicates it; so the first (عن) is attached to the overt (يتساءلون) and the second to the implied one.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying (مهادا): the second object of (جعل), and likewise (أوتادا) and likewise (سباتا), because (جعل) means "made into" (صيّر); likewise (لباسا) and (معاشا).
His saying (وخلقناكم أزواجا): (أزواجا) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We originated you differing: males and females, short and tall". (خلق) means "originated", which is why it passes to only one object.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (سراجا): an object of (جعلنا), which here means "We created"; it too passes to one object, and it does not mean "We made into" as in what preceded.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying (ألفافا): it is the plural of (لف); one says (نبات لف) and (لفيف) when it is dense. It is also said that it is a plural of a plural, as if the singular were (لفاء) and (ألف), like (حمراء) and (أحمر); then (لفاء) is pluralised as (لف), as you say (حمراء) and (حمر); then (لف) is pluralised as (ألفاف), as you say (قفل) and (أقفال).

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying (يوم ينفخ): a badal (substitute) from the first (يوم).
His saying (أفواجا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (تأتون).

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying (لابثين فيها أحقابا): (أحقابا) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān). Whoever reads it (لبثين) likened it to what is an innate quality in man, such as (حذر) "wary" and (فرق) "fearful"; this is far-fetched, because tarrying is not among what is an innate quality in man, and the pattern faʿil is only for what is innate in a thing, and tarrying is not innate. (أحقاب) is an adverbial in both aspects.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying (لا يذوقون): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (لابثين). It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of (أحقاب); it bears the pronoun because it is a verb, so making it overt is not necessary, even though it runs as an adjective of something other than what it belongs to. It is permissible for it to be a naʿt of (أحقاب) only because of the pronoun in (فيها) referring back to (الأحقاب). Had an active participle been in the position of (يذوقون), it would have been necessary to make the pronoun overt if you made it an adjective of (أحقاب).

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (إلا حميما): a badal (substitute) from (برد) if you take (البرد) from coolness. If you make it sleep, then (إلا حميما) is an exception not of the same kind as the first.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying (كذابا): whoever reads it with doubling makes it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of (كذب) [kadhdhaba], with the alif added in it as it was added in (إكراما). As for their saying (تكذيبا), they made the tāʾ a compensation for the doubling of the ʿayn and the yāʾ a substitute for the alif, altering its beginning as they altered its end. The origin of the maṣdar of a quadriliteral verb is to come with the number of letters of the past, with an added alif and a change of vowels. They also said (تكلما), so the maṣdar came with the number of letters of the past without an added alif, and that is because of its many letters; the lām was given ḍamma and not kasra because there is no noun in the language on the pattern tafaʿʿil, and they did not give it fatḥa lest it resemble the past. Al-Kisāʾī read it (كذابا) without doubling, making it the maṣdar of (كاذب كذابا) [Translator's note: printed «مصدرى»]. It is also said that it is the maṣdar of (كذب), as you say (كتبت كتابا).

mekki-muskil:29-29.t:
His saying (وكل شيء أحصيناه كتابا): (كتاب) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because (أحصيناه) means "We wrote it". (كل) is accusative with an implied verb, i.e. "And We enumerated everything — We enumerated it". The nominative is permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying (جزاء وعطاء): two maṣdars, and (حسابا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (عطاء).
His saying (رب السموات): whoever reads it in the nominative and (الرحمن) in the genitive takes it with an implied (هو), and (الرحمن) is a naʿt of (ربك). Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a badal (substitute) from (ربك). Whoever reads it in the nominative and (الرحمن) in the nominative makes it a mubtadaʾ and (الرحمن) its khabar (predicate), or a naʿt of it, with (لا يملكون) the khabar. Whoever reads (الرحمن) in the genitive and (رب) in the nominative makes it a naʿt of (ربك). Whoever reads (الرحمن) in the genitive and (رب) in the genitive makes it a naʿt of (رب), and (رب السموات) is a badal from (ربك). Whoever reads (رب) in the genitive and (الرحمن) in the nominative puts it in the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Most Merciful", or, if you wish, as a mubtadaʾ with (لا يملكون) as the khabar.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t:
His saying (صفا لا يتكلمون): two ḥāls (circumstantials).
His saying (إلا من أذن له الرحمن): (من) is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in (يتكلمون), or in the position of the accusative as an exception.
